scores.why: The vault hides inside working decoy apps and opens with a user-chosen in-app action, with a hash chain, trusted timestamps and a verifier anyone can run without the app. Disguised-evidence apps exist, but not with this verifiability.
Targets domestic and economic violence against women, grounded in Polish law and the Blue Card procedure, with EU statistics and a measurable pilot plan.
Offline, quick exit, auto-lock, helpline numbers and an explicit threat model; held back by a bundled AI key, screenshot blocking disabled for the demo, and the need for an NGO pilot.
Six fully built decoy apps with their own palettes and icons plus a light/dark vault theme; no screenshots in the repo.
About 11k lines of app code and 89 tests covering crypto, chain, timestamps and legal rules; encrypted capture, PDF/ZIP export and the verifier all exist.

projects.built_during_event: unclear: one 30k-line first commit at 20:21 CEST Saturday, then 10 commits until 08:33 Sunday
strengths: Threat model built around an abuser with phone access
Evidence integrity verifiable without the app
Rule-based severity that AI cannot lower; names pseudonymised before AI calls
Strong legal research and honest limits
weaknesses: AI called straight from the phone with a bundled key
red_flags: Monolithic first commit, event-time work unverifiable
Stale proxy code contradicts the README
projects.verdict: An exceptional, deeply considered and well-tested build that fits the brief closely.

scores.why: Role-model stories and chat for girls considering tech studies is common; matching is a simple additive score over 3 profiles.
Aims directly at the gender gap in tech education; no need data or impact metrics.
Three hardcoded students and a chat that never delivers messages; no mentor onboarding, moderation or safeguarding.
Cohesive, polished mobile UI with good hierarchy; AI-looking portraits and a somewhat generic look.
About 3.7k lines, half CSS; front-end-only PWA, no tests, no backend.

projects.built_during_event: unclear: 6k-line file dump at 00:44 CEST Sunday; agent notes describe an earlier app
weaknesses: No way to grow or verify mentors
red_flags: Bulk code dump suggests an earlier codebase
projects.verdict: A pretty, on-theme front-end mock with thin functionality and a common idea.

scores.why: A standard two-sided marketplace matching apprentices with craft masters; the women angle is implied only by the feminine name.
No mention of women or gender barriers anywhere in the code, README or spec.
Real auth, row-level security, distance search and request/review flows, deployed; no verification of masters or protection for young apprentices.
Distinctive wood-plank craft theme ported from design boards; renders cleanly on mobile.
About 1.6k lines; core flows work end to end; no tests, chat out of scope.

red_flags: No women-focused content despite the ImpactHer framing
No AI-use disclosure though commits show AI co-authorship
projects.verdict: A competent, nicely styled apprenticeship marketplace that does not address a problem specific to women. The team's other repo, PiszuPiszu, is unrelated to ImpactHer.

calibration_note: Sejf's 83 reflects exceptional depth and category fit; the other two are typical-to-weak prototypes separated by category fit.
